One weekend. Six small steps.

No prep. You read the steps — your child dreams, directs and tests.

Dream it

Three questions first: Who’s the hero? Where? How do you win?

Ask the machine

Your child describes it — AI builds it. They give the orders.

Play the first version

Play it as-is. First versions are rough — cheer what already works.

Test like a game designer

What’s fun? Too hard? What changes first? That thinking is the lesson.

Improve, one change at a time

“Slower shark.” “Add a score.” One instruction — play again.

Put it online & share it

The game lives on a link — playable anywhere, nothing to install. Send it to grandma.

Who it’s not for

Anti-screen-time or anti-AI families. Young kids do need limited tech time — always supervised. That’s the point: you use the guide to lead them, so tech benefits them, not harms them.

The guide’s limits

Free tools only — currently in the USA & Canada. Paid tools exist; they’re just not in this guide. Use the free ways big tech already offers. You may already pay for AI at work — at home, save the credits.
